rows.name: Qur'an
rows.detail: No direct verse — jurists cite the shared root darb fi'l-ard (travelling for livelihood) as wording-level support only.
rows.detail_long: Ibn Hazm's verdict stands: qirad rests on consensus, not text. The darb-fi'l-ard verses (73:20, 2:198, 62:10) share vocabulary with mudarabah but legislate nothing about it.

rows.display_note: Practice pre-dates revelation; placed at period start
rows.name: Prophetic practice (Khadija trade)
rows.detail: The Prophet traded for Khadija on qirad terms before prophethood and later approved the practice.
rows.detail_long: The sira records the young Muhammad trading Khadija's capital for a profit share — mudarabah's living precedent, approved by his later silence and the Companions' practice.

rows.display_note: Shown at 622 CE; app dating range 622–640 CE, confidence medium
rows.name: Sunan Ibn Majah 2289
rows.detail: 'Three things carry blessing: deferred-payment sale, muqaradah (profit-sharing), mixing wheat with barley for the house' — graded Da'eef in the app.
rows.detail_long: The one hadith naming profit-sharing directly — and the app's own grading is Da'eef (weak), so it is support, not proof. Mudarabah's real weight is Companion practice: Umar, Uthman, Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Aisha invested orphans' funds this way. App dating 622-640 CE, medium confidence.
rows.internal_ref: Record + grading pulled from app hadith file (kafalah_source_extract.json session)

rows.timeline_year_basis: app dating block: range 622-632 (Madinan), displayed at range earliest per rule
rows.display_note: Companion-era investor conditions — the earliest risk covenants on record
rows.name: Bulugh al-Maram 1043
rows.detail: Muqaradah risk conditions. Hakim ibn Hizam's muqaradah covenants: no livestock, no sea transport, no river-bed camps — breach them and you guarantee my capital.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: capital handed over for muqaradah (profit shared) under named prohibitions — trading in living beings, carrying it by sea, settling at a river bottom — with liability shifting to the agent on breach. Investor risk restrictions and a breach-triggers-guarantee clause, in the first generation. The direct ancestor of every mudarabah investment-restriction schedule.
rows.evidence_display: Bulugh al-Maram 1043 (text + dating block in app)

rows.timeline_year_basis: app dating block: range 622-632 (Madinan), displayed at range earliest per rule
rows.display_note: Transmitted by Ibn Majah per the app text; muqarada glossed in the record itself
rows.name: Mishkat al-Masabih 2815
rows.detail: Muqarada among the blessed things. Muqarada named among blessed practices: deferred-term sale, muqarada, and mixing wheat with barley for the household, not for sale.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim (Suhaib; Ibn Majah transmitted): the record lists muqarada with its own gloss — 'giving someone some property to trade with, the profit being shared between the two, but any loss falling on the property.' Profit shared, loss on capital: the mudarabah loss rule stated inside the hadith corpus itself.

rows.display_note: Sahih in the app. Bridge row: the hadith corpus recording COURT practice on mudarabah
rows.name: Sunan an-Nasa'i 3967

hadith_meta.narrator: Muhammad (ibn Sirin), on the judge Shuraih

rows.detail: Shuraih's two rulings on mudarabah disputes. Judge Shuraih's complete mudarabah case law: the agent proves calamity to be excused; the investor proves betrayal, else the agent's oath stands.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: 'I do not know that Shuraih ever ruled on Mudarabah disputes except in two ways' — burden of proof on the mudarib for loss-by-calamity, burden on the investor for breach-of-trust, the agent's oath sufficing otherwise. Evidence law for profit-sharing disputes, already settled in the first century and preserved with a Sahih grading.
rows.evidence_display: Sunan an-Nasa'i 3967 (text + grading + dating block in app)
rows.internal_ref: Record read verbatim from app hadith file (batch2_source_extract_new.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.timeline_year_basis: app dating block: range 632-661 (rule: umar ibn al-khattab), displayed at range earliest
rows.display_note: The founding case: retroactive qirad, principal + half profit to the treasury
rows.name: Muwatta 1450

hadith_meta.narrator: Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father

rows.detail: Umar converts his sons' windfall into qirad. Abu Musa lends state money to Umar's sons; they trade and profit; Umar rules it qirad — treasury takes principal plus half the profit.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: the sons of Umar carry public funds from Basra, buy Iraqi wares, sell in Madina at profit. Umar objects that the loan came only because of who they were; Ubaydullah answers that they bore the guarantee had it perished. A bystander proposes: 'make it a qirad.' Umar does — principal and half-profit to the treasury, half-profit to the traders. The canonical origin case for capital-labour profit splitting.
rows.evidence_display: Muwatta 1450, Qirad chapter (text + dating block in app)
rows.internal_ref: Record read verbatim from app hadith file (batch2_source_extract_new.json, 2026-07-14)

hadith_meta.narrator: al-Ala ibn Abd ar-Rahman, from his father, from his father

rows.detail: Uthman gives money as qirad. Uthman ibn Affan gives capital as qirad on profit-sharing terms — a second caliph practising the contract.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim: 'Uthman ibn Affan gave him some money as qirad to use provided the profit was shared between them.' One line, but a caliph-level precedent independent of Umar's case.

hadith_meta.narrator: abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Imam al-Sadiq
topics_app: Liability for Profit Sharing, Its Profit and Expenses (Al-Mudarabah)

rows.detail: Mudarabah liability chapter. Imam al-Sadiq: the working partner takes his profit share but bears no loss — unless he violates the owner's instructions.
rows.detail_long: App text read verbatim, from a chapter titled 'Liability for Profit Sharing, Its Profit and Expenses (Al-Mudarabah)': the mudarib 'can have (his share of) the profit but is not liable for depreciation (loss) unless he violates the instructions of the owner of the assets.' The same loss-on-capital / breach-shifts-liability structure as the Sunni line — stated from the Imami side.
rows.internal_ref: Record read verbatim from app hadith file (batch2_source_extract_new.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: Malik ibn Anas
rows.detail: Malik's al-Muwatta, Book of Qirad — the earliest systematic record, with Uthman's qirad deal and Umar's sons trading public money.
rows.detail_long: Kitab al-Qirad preserves the founding cases: Uthman funding a trader for half the profit, and Umar converting his sons' windfall into the first recorded qirad ruling. App book F0778-B01. ENRICHED THIS SESSION — Muwatta Qirad chapter read verbatim: 1452 defines the recognised qirad (no guarantee by the agent; travel food/clothing from capital when it can bear it); 1453 disapproves converting an unpaid debt into qirad before repossession — 'the debtor may be in a tight situation, and want to delay it to increase it'; 1455 bans either party stipulating any exclusive gain — 'no sale, no rent, no work, no advance' reserved to one side without the other sharing.
rows.internal_ref: saa.pdf p.3; figure + book confirmed in app | Muwatta 1452/1453/1455 read verbatim (batch2_source_extract_new.json, 2026-07-14)

rows.name: al-Sarakhsi
rows.detail: Al-Sarakhsi's al-Mabsut gives the fullest early Hanafi treatment of mudarabah.
rows.detail_long: The Mabsut's mudarabah book works through capital conditions, permitted manager actions and profit-split rules — the systematic Hanafi doctrine. App book F0333-B50.
rows.internal_ref: saa.pdf p.3; figure + book confirmed in app

rows.name: al-Kasani
rows.detail: Al-Kasani: strict analogy would forbid mudarabah — it stands on consensus and need.
rows.detail_long: Bada'i concedes qiyas would void mudarabah (undefined labor for undefined wage) and validates it by ijma' and people's need — the classic case of consensus overriding analogy. Finance-local figure.

rows.name: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi
rows.detail: Ibn Qudama treats mudarabah extensively for the Hanbalis.
rows.detail_long: Al-Mughni's treatment covers capital, management and loss rules for the Hanbali school. App book F0749-B50.
rows.internal_ref: saa.pdf p.3; figure + book confirmed in app

rows.name: al-Tabari
rows.detail: Commentary attaches to the darb-fi'l-ard verses but treats the link as wording only, not legal proof.
rows.detail_long: Al-Tabari on 73:20 (7,200+ chars in the app file) reads 'others travelling the land seeking Allah's bounty' as those journeying for trade and earnings — vocabulary shared with mudarabah, but no contract ruling drawn from it. Confirms the contract's basis lies in practice and consensus, not this verse.
rows.evidence_display: Jami' al-Bayan (Tafsir al-Tabari), on Q73:20 (text in app)
rows.internal_ref: Passage read verbatim this session from app tafsir file (batch2_source_extract.json)

rows.name: Mohammad Nejatullah Siddiqi
rows.work_title: Partnership and Profit-Sharing in Islamic Law
rows.detail: Siddiqi's 'Partnership and Profit-Sharing in Islamic Law' — the seminal modern theory; basis of two-tier deposit banking.
rows.detail_long: Siddiqi formalizes mudarabah as the engine of interest-free banking: depositors as rabb al-mal, the bank as mudarib, then the bank re-deploying funds as rabb al-mal — the two-tier model every Islamic bank charter cites.
rows.evidence_display: Siddiqi's 'Partnership and Profit-Sharing in Islamic Law'

rows.timeline_year_basis: adopted Shari'ah Board meeting 8, Al-Madinah, 28 Safar-4 Rabi' I 1423 / 11-16 May 2002
rows.name: AAOIFI
rows.detail: AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard No. 13 codifies mudarabah (investment and savings deposits).
rows.detail_long: SS13 sets capital, profit-distribution and loss rules for deposit-side mudarabah. VERIFIED: adopted 16 May 2002. CLAUSES VERIFIED-TO-TEXT (SS13, ss1.txt, 2026-07-14): 8/8 the mudarib's profit share arises once profit is realised, subject to retention rules; the mudarib bears no losses except on breach of trust — misconduct, negligence or breach of the mudarabah terms; 9/1 in unrestricted mudarabah the mudarib may do what entrepreneurs in his field do; guarantees from the mudarib may cover only negligence, misconduct or breach.
rows.internal_ref: Verified from the official AAOIFI Shari'ah Standards 2015 full text (user-supplied PDF, adoption page read this session) | SS13 clauses read verbatim from ss1.txt (2026-07-14)

rows.timeline_year_basis: current period marker (2024), mirrors lineage_v4 current_status convention
rows.name: Industry practice
rows.detail: Mudarabah survives mainly on the deposit side (investment accounts) and in sukuk; pure two-tier mudarabah banking remains rare.
rows.detail_long: Modern usage: unrestricted investment accounts (bank as mudarib), mudarabah sukuk, and fund structures — while financing-side mudarabah stays thin because of the no-collateral, no-guaranteed-return core.
